chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma'il al-Munqari, from his grandfather Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:

Whoever eats clay, itching will occur in his body, he will suffer hemorrhoids, a bad malady will be stirred up in him, and strength will be taken from his legs and feet; and whatever is diminished from his deeds in the time between him and his health before eating it, he will be held accountable for it and punished for it.

key_terms.البواسير: Hemorrhoids — a digestive/vascular condition caused by eating clay
key_terms.الحكة: Itching — a skin ailment resulting from eating clay
key_terms.الطين: Clay/dirt — the substance being prohibited from consumption
key_terms.حوسب عليه: He will be held accountable — the missed worship obligations will be counted against him on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.داء السوء: A bad malady — referring to chronic or serious illness

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about eating clay or dirt in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS), the fifth Imam, prohibits eating clay (al-tin) and warns of its severe physical and spiritual consequences: bodily itching, hemorrhoids, chronic illness, and loss of strength in the limbs. The Imam further declares that any acts of worship missed due to the illness resulting from eating clay will be reckoned against the person and punished. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that intentionally harming one's body is spiritually blameworthy.
word_analysis: and it will cause him to inherit/suffer
